## Summary

Under section 96(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, the maximum gap between the date of one annual general meeting and the next is **fifteen months**.

The Registrar may extend the time for holding an AGM, other than the first AGM, by a period not exceeding **three months** for any special reason.

This is legal information, not legal advice. Legal currentness is unverified.

## Summary

An auditor appointed at an annual general meeting holds office **from the conclusion of that meeting until the conclusion of the sixth annual general meeting**, with the meeting at which the appointment is made counted as the first meeting.

Legal currentness is unverified. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Relevant quotation

“The auditor appointed in the annual general meeting shall hold office from the conclusion of that meeting till the conclusion of the sixth annual general meeting, with the meeting wherein such appointment has been made being counted as the first meeting.”

## Summary

Under the Trade Marks Act, 1999, a “trade mark” means a mark that:

- Is capable of being represented graphically; and
- Is capable of distinguishing one person’s goods or services from those of others.

It may include the shape of goods, their packaging, and a combination of colours.

The definition also covers marks used or proposed to be used in trade to indicate a connection between goods or services and a person entitled to use the mark. It includes certification trade marks and collective marks.

Legal currentness is unverified. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Relevant quotation

“trade mark” means a mark capable of being represented graphically and which is capable of distinguishing the goods or services of one person from those of others and may include shape of goods, their packaging and combination of colours.
The supplied evidence does not state the right conferred on a registered proprietor under the relevant provision, including the exclusive right to use the trade mark.
missingFacts: exclusive right to the use of the trade mark
